source_span: to me, the 'far and away' standout-story about yesterday was the absolutely epic 'Vol Crush'...and what that mechanically meant for 'Higher Stocks'
source_chain: Dealers came into Monday short puts/OTM puts (after Thursday's record CBOE put-buying day) with VIX falling 28->20 in ~2.5 sessions, therefore those puts lost delta twice (spot up, vol down) forcing dealers to buy back shorted futures hedges, making 'a huge chunk' of the breadth rally mechanical rather than real demand, therefore 'here today, as the Vol meltdown has stalled-out, so too has the Stock rally' -- invalidation: the vol-crush engine stalling (which is what happened once Tuesday's hot CPI print killed the vol collapse) ends the forced-buying rally.
pulse_chain: Dealers came into the week short puts after Thursday's record CBOE put-buying, so as prices rose and the cost of protection collapsed (VIX 28->20 in ~2.5 sessions) those positions lost value fast enough to force dealers to buy back shorted futures hedges, therefore Monday's broad advance (424/503 higher) was 'machinery, not conviction' with McElligott reading the vol collapse, not the breadth, as the real story, therefore Tuesday's hot CPI (core 0.3% vs 0.2% expected) stopped the vol meltdown and took the rally down with it -- invalidation: the vol-crush stalling (triggered by the CPI miss) ends the mechanical bid, matching the note's own stall-equals-stall claim.
why: The pulse reproduces McElligott's exact A-therefore-B-therefore-C argument (short puts + vol crush -> forced dealer hedge-buying -> mechanical rally -> vol-crush stall ends the rally) with the same attribution to Nomura and the same invalidation condition, and layers the surrounding bank debate (UBS, JPMorgan, BTIG, Morgan Stanley, Goldman's CTA pivot levels and buyback flow) with figures and sourcing that check out against each named desk's actual note, so no step is reversed, no bank is swapped, and no invented mechanism replaces what the notes argue.
